reasoning: B fixes every reported symptom with the methods the LibMP guide recommends: a snapshot instead of pausing, EmitThreadFrameEnd with EnterTimestampFrameLocal, and GPU time from the GPU thread's scopes. It also fixes all the unreported misuses and passes every check. A has a sound pause/resume structure and a workable overlap split, but it still leaks the GetCounterSamples array, still reports GPU spans that are far wider than the frame, skips stack level 0 when checking for nested Physics scopes, and fails StyLua.

criteria.note: It opens its own session with `LibMP.Session.OpenFromLiveData()` while capture is paused, disposes it after `pcall(buildReport, session)`, and no longer uses `FpsOverlay.getSession()`.

criteria.criterion: Leaves the shared profiler as it found it
criteria.note: Capture comes back on every path: on open failure, and after the pcall even when it fails. It drops the `SetFrameLimit(256)` call entirely.

criteria.criterion: Per-frame scope times clipped to frame
criteria.note: `distribute` splits each enter/exit interval across the overlapping frame spans, so no frame gets more scope time than it lasted. Underflowed scopes, scopes still open at the end, and the missing warm-up frame lose a little time at the edges.
It checks the ancestors for a Physics-group timer and counts only the outermost scope. The loop `for ancestorDepth = 1, depth - 1` skips stack level 0, though, even though the stack is 0-based.
It uses `tickToMsGpu` and clamps negative spans with `math.max(0, ...)`. Spans far wider than the frame are still reported as-is, and it does not use the GPU thread.

It switches to `FetchTimerDesc` and hoists `FindGroupId`. `session:GetCounterSamples(heapId):FetchLastSample()` still leaks the array, and `if heapId` and `assert(mainThreadId)` never catch a 0 result, because 0 is truthy in Luau.
The report fields are kept and FpsOverlay is untouched. Incomplete frames are now left out, and StyLua fails on the long `table.insert(spans, ...)` line.
It takes a snapshot with `CaptureToBufferSync`, opens it with `OpenFromBuffer`, disposes that session, and never touches the overlay's session.

criteria.criterion: Leaves the shared profiler as it found it
criteria.note: It never pauses capture. It sets the limit to 256 for the capture and restores `FpsOverlay.FrameLimit` afterwards, even when the capture fails, because the capture call is wrapped in a pcall.

criteria.criterion: Per-frame scope times clipped to frame
criteria.note: It uses `EmitThreadFrameEnd` with `EnterTimestampFrameLocal`, takes the frame start for underflowed exits, and starts one frame early to warm up the stack.
The `openPhysicsScopes` counter adds a Physics scope only when it is outermost, and the stack walk at frame end uses an `isPhysicsCounted` flag.
It sums the top-level scopes on the GPU thread (`GetThreadIdGpu`, depth 0) with `tickToMsGpu` and no longer relies on the frame's GPU ticks.
It uses `FetchTimerDesc`, finds the Physics group once, uses `FetchLastCounterSample`, compares IDs with `~= 0`, and reads each view before the next fetch.
The fields and FpsOverlay are unchanged and all checks pass. `run()` now waits about 122 frames, and `isPhysics` fetches the timer description on every call instead of caching it.

strengths: Clean pause/resume, with the session disposed on every path
Does not touch the frame limit at all
Splitting scopes by frame-span overlap is valid in principle
weaknesses: Spans far wider than the frame are still reported as GPU time
The ancestor scan misses stack level 0
Truthiness checks on Find*** results never catch 0

strengths: Reads from a snapshot, so capture is never paused
Restores the frame limit, even when the capture errors
Clips scopes per frame with the method the guide recommends
Measures GPU time from the GPU thread
Guards against two reports running at once
weaknesses: The report now waits about 2 seconds
Changing the frame limit temporarily clears the overlay's counter history
Group lookups for timers are not cached
